title: Scaling economics snapshot & forecast playbook
body:
Executive summary:
This is a working snapshot for near-term (6mo) capacity planning that feeds Optimize recommendations. It is intentionally lightweight and spreadsheet-first: rows are scenario slices, columns capture traffic, efficiency levers, and resulting GPU counts/costs. Goal: produce a 6-week action list (autoscale params, cache rules, quantization targets) tied to dollar/runway impact.

Key assumptions (configurable):
- Avg tokens per request (end-to-end, incl. prompt + completion): 320 tokens
- Avg sequence length for scheduling: 512
- Peak RPS baseline (today): 45 rps
- Throughput per GPU (target util 65%, FP16, medium batch): 18k tokens/s
- Monthly cost per GPU instance (including infra + license): $8,100
- Cache hit reduces token compute by 60% for repeated prefixes
- Quantization (8-bit) reduces cost per token by ~28% at mild quality degradation

Scenario table (sample model: open-slim-v2):
Scenario | Start RPS | Growth mo | 6-mo RPS | Target util | Required GPUs formula | Required GPUs (calc) | Monthly GPU cost | Cache savings | Net monthly cost
Baseline | 45 | 3% | 52 | 65% | ceil((RPS*avg_tokens)/(throughput*util)) | 6 | $48,600 | -$6,000 | $42,600
Product-led growth | 45 | 18% | 123 | 70% | same | 14 | $113,400 | -$15,600 | $97,800
Holiday spike | 45 | spike to 250 (week) | 250 | 80% | peak-surge model (burst) | 29 (burst reserve) | $234,900 | -$28,000 | $206,900
Notes on table numbers: the throughput formula used: throughput_effective = throughput_per_gpu * util. Required GPUs = ceil((RPS * avg_tokens) / throughput_effective). Monthly GPU cost uses committed pricing approximation; burst capacity uses short-term on-demand uplift factor x1.85. Cache savings are estimated by applying hit-rate*token_reduction*effective_cost_per_token over monthly token volume.

Sensitivity slices to include in final sheet (columns to add):
- Avg tokens ±20%
- Throughput per GPU ±15% (kernel/compiler improvements)
- Cache hit rate 0–60%
- Quantization efficiency options (FP16, INT8, GPTQ)
- Region mix (NA vs EU) - cost multiplier

Operational levers and estimated unit economics (quick):
1) Autoscale policy tightening: lower min instances, faster scale-down = potential -7% monthly cost but risks cold-start latency.
2) Prefix caching rules (aggressive prune + TTL 6h): expected hit rate uplift +20pp for high-repeat flows -> ~12–18% cost reduction on those routes.
3) Quantization pilot on low-risk models: target 8-bit for non-chat read-only workloads -> immediate -20–30% cost per token.
4) Request shaping / token limits on free tiers: simple cap to reduce tail cost spikes (saves ~3–6% overall).

Short worked example (Baseline -> apply two levers):
- Baseline GPUs: 6, monthly cost $48,600.
- Add prefix caching (net -12% on compute bill for cached routes) => effective monthly -$5,832.
- Deploy INT8 for offline embedding model (20% of tokens) => additional -$1,944.
- Net monthly cost ~ $40,824 (-16%).

Open questions / uncertainties to resolve in sheet: 
- Confirm throughput per GPU for open-slim-v2 at sequence=512 under our kernel set (ticket: JIRA-INF-279).
- Clarify burst pricing multiplier for cloud-reserve contracts vs marketplace.
- Measure current real-world cache hit rate per route (telemetry query: analytics.cache.route-hit-rate last 90d).

Actionable next steps (6-week):
- Week 1: instrument and export per-route token volumes and cache hit rate (owner: Lin).
- Week 2: run microbench (throughput measurements) for open-slim-v2 and quantized variants (owner: Marc).
- Week 3: simulate autoscale policy changes in staging with synthetic traffic (owner: SRE - Sofia).
- Week 4-6: implement prefix-caching rules for top-5 routes, measure delta, roll to prod if stable.

Appendix: quick formulas to paste into spreadsheet cells
- throughput_effective = throughput_per_gpu * target_util
- required_gpus = CEILING((rps * avg_tokens) / throughput_effective, 1)
- monthly_cost = required_gpus * gpu_monthly_rate + reserved_overhead + datastore_costs
- net_cost_after_cache = monthly_cost * (1 - estimated_cache_savings_pct)

Thoughts / heuristics (notes to self):
- For early-stage customers, prefer burst strategy + cache over large committed reserve; for enterprises on Dedicated, commit to lower unit price but require stronger SLAs.
- Present 3 action slabs in Optimize: Quick wins (cache, shaping), Medium (quantize), Structural (contract renegotiation, dedicated pools).

Backlinks / references: see linked artifacts for PR and ticket numbers, also cross-ref: shared_drives/product/optimize/workload-shape-headroom-matrix-quicklook.json (for historical shape buckets).

Draft status: rough numbers, intended as the single-sheet source-of-truth to feed the cost-recommendation engine. Pls leave inline comments in the sheet; will iterate once microbench results arrive.
